correctness.rationale: In a tree the unique-path probability of connection is \(p^{d}\), giving the exact cross-cut intervention gain \(2F_e(p)/n\). Complete Prüfer enumeration covers every \(n^{n-2}\) labeled tree for each \(2\le n\le7\); exact integer distance polynomials and rational Bernstein coefficients certify a fixed winning edge in each tree for every \(p\in[0,1]\), not merely sampled probabilities. In the eight-vertex witness, the exact differences are \(F_h-F_m=p^2(1-2p)\), \(F_h-F_{\ell}=p^2(1+2p+3p^2+2p^3)\), and \(F_m-F_{\ell}=p^3(4+3p+2p^2)\), proving the unique switching threshold and the full optimizer sets. The standalone checker replays all exact finite certificate checks, and independent direct bond-percolation enumerations provide a separate verification of the example. No assertion beyond the stated tree order/domain is made.

value.rationale: Edge removal is a natural unit-cost network intervention. At low transmissibility the intervention impact depends on short distance-2 paths, while near p=1 it depends on the cut-size product. This creates a fundamental tension between local transmission suppression and global connectivity severance. The theorem identifies the exact smallest tree supporting a change in the optimal intervention, establishes the complete absence of change in every smaller tree, and gives an interpretable eight-vertex witness. The bound distinguishes a natural decision question rather than an arbitrary fixed-parameter polynomial computation; finite results have stand-alone benchmark value. No policy or larger-graph extrapolation is asserted.
